source_document.body:
AI
Mobile
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Front Angled 3
Amid the many trends and stories shaping the hardware world in 2026, the final quarter shows a confluence of several influences. AI continues to loom over everything this year, both client and server, and 2026 picks up where 2025 left off, with an even heavier emphasis on inference. Meanwhile, Microsoft’s latest efforts to bootstrap its Windows-on-Arm ecosystem are making good progress, thanks to another generation of improvements to its x86-on-Arm Prism emulator. And finally, amid all this, the client hardware market is trying to make sense (and cents) of a run-up in DRAM and NAND prices.
As we enter the fall, these trends conveniently converge in a single device: Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra. The company’s latest-generation flagship Surface laptop, the Ultra, is unlike anything that came before it, with Microsoft going above and beyond to develop a high-end laptop that, well, can go above and beyond itself. All the while, they are staking the fate of their new flagship laptop on the Arm architecture, which is still finding its footing in the Windows world.
As a result, the Surface Laptop Ultra is a culmination of several firsts for Microsoft. As a complete product, it is the company’s most direct take on (or competitor to) Apple’s MacBook Pro lineup yet, making a direct play on the high-end market that Apple has captured so much of over the last several years. Meanwhile, this is one of the first-generation Windows laptops to ship with NVIDIA’s RTX Spark SoC, the consumer branding for their high-performance GB10 SoC that we have seen in numerous developer-focused mini-PCs over the last year. Finally, it is one of Microsoft’s biggest hardware releases for the developer market in at least the last several years, as Microsoft seeks to further bootstrap developers with all the tools they need to make the next generation of Windows applications.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra Key Specs (As Configured)
Processor | NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X 20-core
Operating System | Windows 11 Pro
Memory | 128GB LPDDR5X
Storage | 1TB SSD (M.2 2280, PCIe Gen5)
GPU Options | NVIDIA Integrated Blackwell RTX 5120 GPU core
Display | 15-Inch PixelSense, 3270×2180 120Hz, 2000nits Max Brightness, 100% DCI, Touchscreen
Battery | 92Wh
Form Factor | Laptop
Dimensions | 328.8 x 238.7 x 19.16 mm (12.95 x 9.40 x 0.75 in)
Weight | 2.0 kg (4.41 lbs)
Wireless | Wi-Fi 7 + Bluetooth 5.4
Colors | Platinum (Gray) Nightfall (Black)
Ports | Left : 1x HDMI 2.1b, 2x USB-C 40Gbps, 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack Right: 1x USB-C 40Gbps (Magnetic Connect), 1x USB-A 10Gbps, SD Card Reader
As a result, although this is far from Microsoft’s first Surface device, first Arm-on-Windows device, or even their first productivity laptop, the Surface Laptop Ultra is potentially the most important device launch from them in years. If it succeeds, it will shape the Surface ecosystem for years to come. If it does not, it will end up in the footnote pile next to 2012’s Surface RT (which we used at STH). The Surface Laptop Ultra is not meant to (nor will it) be a game changer for the broader laptop market, but it is still a significant launch for Microsoft’s hardware division.
Meanwhile, for partner/supplier NVIDIA, although this is far from the first GB10 device on the market, the Ultra is one of a wave of laptops that marks the first time the chip has made it out of a mini-PC and into a laptop. NVIDIA has wanted to break into the market as a CPU/SoC supplier for years. This is their first chance in several years to do that. But how well will the N1X sibling to the GB10 translate into powering a Windows laptop? That is one of the questions we will have to answer today.
Quick note : You may notice Ryan Smith wrote the first half of this review, and Patrick wrote the second half. Again, we had a week, and we were at OCP 2026 all week covering that show. So without any further ado, let us jump right in.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra External Hardware Overview
When it comes to the Surface Laptop Ultra’s design, there is no dancing around the fact that this is meant to be Microsoft’s answer to the MacBook Pro. So we can only address it head-on. Microsoft wants to compete with Apple’s flagship laptops, and this is what they think a Windows equivalent should look and behave like.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Front 1
Microsoft is no stranger to designing laptops, of course. Their mainstream Surface laptops are already up to their 8 th generation, and the Surface Pro 2-in-1s are too. But the company needs to step up its game with the Ultra. They are building a premium laptop, packing a more powerful SoC, and charging a higher price than ever.
The 15-inch laptop is meant to straddle the line between being a productivity laptop and a portable laptop. It is a bit too small to be a desktop replacement-class laptop, which means it is reasonably portable. But it is not a thin and light ultraportable like the smaller mainstream Surface Laptops. Instead, at 19mm thick and weighing 2kg on the dot, this laptop fits the developer-on-the-go mindset.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Rear 1
Microsoft is offering a few different configurations of the Surface Laptop Ultra. Most notably, a choice between 18- and 20-core versions of NVIDIA’s RTX Spark N1X processor. Regardless of configuration, there is only one body and one size available. This is not a laptop lineup bifurcated by size, at least not yet.
Surface-Laptop-Ultra-Ports-Side-by-side
The body itself is made from aluminum, which is pretty standard fare these days for premium laptops. Microsoft offers it in either a “Platinum” (grey) finish, as seen with our review sample, or a “Nightfall” (black) finish. Many configurations are available in both colors, but on Microsoft’s pre-order website, Nightfall seems to be treated as the more premium option, since you cannot currently order a laptop with more than 32GB of RAM in the Platinum finish.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Front 2
All Surface Laptop Ultras ship with the same display. This is a 15-inch high-DPI 3270×2180 “PixelSense” touchscreen LCD display. According to Microsoft, the HDR-capable display can reach an eye-searing max brightness of 2000 nits and cover the full DCI-P3 color space. For developers who need a bit more fluidity (or want to sneak in some gaming), the display also supports variable refresh rates up to 120Hz. Since this is a premium laptop, Microsoft color-calibrates the panels individually. It is not an OLED, but our STH studio team members who usually use MacBook Pros all thought the display looked sharp. If you really want an OLED for those deep blacks, other manufacturers are making RTX Spark laptops with other screens. Still, this is a touchscreen, which can be useful for many.
On the bottom deck of the laptop, we have Microsoft’s keyboard and haptic trackpad. As is typical for anything above budget laptops these days, this is a fully backlit keyboard. Microsoft is not duplicating Apple’s fingerprint sensor functionality here (relying instead on Windows Hello), so it is a keyboard that is just a keyboard. Meanwhile, according to Microsoft, the Ultra’s touchpad is their largest to date, larger than what is on the mainstream 15-inch Surface Laptop.
And while you can just barely spot it due to the very thin bezel around the LCD panel, Microsoft has embedded a full camera suite along the top edge of the display. At the center is a 1080p “Surface Studio” camera. Meanwhile, IR cameras flank it on either side to support Windows Hello.
For audio, Microsoft built in four downward-firing “OmniSonic” speakers, with two on the left front and two on the right front. Microsoft supports Dolby Atmos here. For users who need more enclosed audio, Microsoft explicitly confirms the laptop supports Bluetooth LE Audio, a feature that is still pretty rare on Windows laptops. Meanwhile, for audio input, there are a pair of microphones built into the body to allow for voice focusing.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Side 1
Meanwhile, when it comes time to plug something into the Surface Laptop Ultra, Microsoft has taken a somewhat restrained approach to the number of available ports. On the left side of the laptop, you will find an HDMI 2.1b port, two 40Gbps USB-C ports, and a 3.5mm combo audio jack. Surprisingly, Microsoft has not opted to secure Thunderbolt 4 certification despite the laptop’s premium focus. Still, at 40Gbps with full DP Alt Mode and 140W charging, these are highly capable USB-C ports. At present, we are still trying to suss out who is providing the controller driving them, as the RTX Spark SoC itself does not support 40Gbps USB speeds.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Side 2
As for the right side of the laptop, things get a bit more interesting. On this side we find 3 ports: a full-size SD card reader, a 10Gbps USB-A port, and a special 40Gbps USB-C port that Microsoft calls its Magnetic Connect port.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Magnetic USB Type-C Charging Cable 2
Replacing Microsoft’s proprietary Surface Connect port from past designs, the company has developed a magnetic USB-C port; Microsoft’s take on Apple’s MagSafe. Whereas MagSafe is only a charging port, the Magnetic Connect port is an upgraded USB-C port, meaning that it can be used for data as well and is otherwise a fully capable USB-C port. The magnetic aspect of the port is technically not the connector itself, but rather it is magnets that Microsoft has placed on either side of the port to help keep the charging cable firmly attached.
Microsoft-Surface-Laptop-Ultra-USB-C-vs-Magnetic-Connect-Ports
To further reinforce the port (or rather, to reduce the chance of breakage), the actual port is larger than a standard USB-C port. The connector inside is still USB-C through and through, but the body is larger to allow it to break away more safely from the intricate 24-pin USB-C connector. While the Ultra can accept a charge on any of its USB-C ports, you would need a standard USB-C cable to plug in to the USB-C ports on the left side.
That is all you will find for I/O ports on the Surface Laptop Ultra. It is less altruistic than some PC OEMs’ workstation laptops, but if we are sticking with the MacBook Pro comparisons, it is almost identical to Apple’s port collection.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Rear Angled 1
Rounding out our laptop look, here is a quick rear view. As we will see in greater detail in our internal teardown, Microsoft is using a pretty standard blower setup, with fans pushing hot air out of the system below the display hinge.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Bottom 1
Finally, here is a shot of the bottom side of the laptop. We will get more into this in a moment, but the bottom of the laptop is exceptionally clean. You will not find any stickers here. Or vents or screw holes, for that matter. Just the Microsoft logo, a model number, and some simple regulatory information printed on to the aluminum plate.
With our tour of the assembled laptop complete, let us crack it open and take a look inside.

How Much Is a Mercedes-AMG GT 63 S Worth in Today’s Used Car Market Stateside?
20 photos
Photo: Instagram | automotive_ambitions
The first-gen Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe is officially dead and buried. In fact, production ceased almost one year ago, and more recently, the three-pointed star brand’s performance-oriented division introduced its successor.
Wearing the same name, it has yet to hit the assembly line, but will will do that soon, reports indicate, and it will come to life at the same Sindelfingen factory in Germany. Unless you’ve been living under a rock these past few months, then you know that this model features a very controversial design on the outside, which has granted it plenty of online hate. And not only does Mercedes not care, but it is expanding the family with a similarly-styled crossover, based on the same underpinnings.
Recent scoops and renderings have created a very clear picture of what this model will look like once it starts gunning for the Porsche Cayenne Electric officially, and you can check out a set of realistic CGIs here . However, before you do that, we should move on to the real reason behind this story. And that’s the GT 4-Door Coupe pictured in the gallery. This is a previous-generation model in the GT 63 S configuration, which means that it packs a healthy V8 engine under the hood, and it is for sale, as you have likely guessed.
With no outside intervention, this model had 630 bhp (639 ps/470 kW) to play with and 664 lb-ft (900 Nm) of torque. That’s how much its familiar 4.0-liter bi-turbocharged V8 engine produced when the car was brand new, channeled to the 4Matic+ all-wheel drive system through a nine-speed automatic transmission. That’s plenty of power for a roomy daily, and the performance is on par with previous-generation supercars, as the 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) acceleration takes only 3.2 seconds. Flat-out, it will do 196 mph (316 kph).
Photo: Instagram | automotive_ambitions Mind you, one should not mistake this model for the Mercedes-AMG GT 63 S E Performance , as this one stands in an even crazier league. It is an absolute force to be reckoned with, as its electrified V8 powertrain churns out a total of 831 bhp (843 ps/620 kW) and 1,033 lb-ft (1,400 Nm) of torque. From 0-62 mph (0-100 kph), this model needs just 2.9 seconds, and that places it just 0.2 seconds behind the Lamborghini Temerario, aka the Raging Bull’s new “baby” supercar. The top speed is identical to the GT 63 S.
As for the new-gen Mercedes-AMG GT 63 4-Door Coupe , it has even more power to play with. Its triple-motor electric powertrain develops a massive 1,153 bhp (1,169 ps/860 kW) and 1,475 Nm (2,000 Nm) of torque. With the one-foot roll-out included, you are looking at 2.1 seconds from 0 to 62 mph. The lesser GT 53 comes with a more down-to-earth 805 bhp (816 ps/600 kW) in total, and is roughly one and a half seconds slower, the spec sheet reveals.
The pictured Mercedes-AMG GT 63 S is a 2021 model year car that features a Designo Graphite Gray Magno exterior paint finish, and Black Exclusive Nappa Leather upholstery on the inside, stitched together with red string for a bit of contrast. It also features the Driver Assistance Package, the Executive Rear Seat Package, AMG Night Package, AMG Exterior Carbon Fiber Package II, AMG Performance Steering Wheel in Dinamica and carbon fiber, a head-up display, AMG Performance seats, a panoramic roof, Burmester audio, etc.
Photo: Instagram | automotive_ambitions According to the ad, this particular car has a clean title, and has seen plenty of action over the years. That’s because the odometer read approximately 67,000 miles (~108,000 km) at the time of cataloging. So, how much is a 2021 model year Mercedes-AMG GT 63 S worth in 2026 in the United States of America? Between $70,000 and $120,000. The value depends on the trim, configuration, mileage, overall condition, and other such factors, and it is basically a mere fraction of what the model used to cost brand new.
The Mercedes-AMG GT 63 S used to start at over $160,000 for the 2021 model year, and the example pictured in the gallery above was a lot more expensive, almost breaking into the $200K territory. The listing claims that the first owner paid $194,860 for this machine. So, how much do you think this ride is worth today? Unless you said $78,991, then you are wrong, because this was the asking price at the time of writing. And that’s 4115,869 less than what it used to cost initially, so depreciation has hit this model like a freight train.
Now, this GT 63 S is definitely a lot of car for the money, and if you dig the way this one looks inside and out, are not afraid of the high maintenance, and the high mileage does not worry you, then you may want to swipe right on it. If you want to do that, then you will have to get in touch with the vendor, @automotive_ambitions on Instagram. This MAN TGE Used to Haul Motocross Bikes — Now It’s a Bold, Head-Turning Home on Wheels
24 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Built Campervans
Today's featured project is based on a MAN TGE, one of the more popular vans in the UK – this one has a long wheelbase and all-wheel-drive (4Motion). It was created by Custom Built Campervans, a UK-based, family-run company specializing in, as you can tell from its name, bespoke mobile homes.
This is a special build in the sense that this rig used to be a camper van designed to haul motocross bikes. The interior did not work for the customer, so they asked Custom Built Campervans to bring their totally different vision to life.
As usual, let's start by taking a look at the outside. This rig's exterior is a head-turner, not only because it sports a variety of upgrades , but also because it's finished in bright orange paint all around. It also has a decal with black and grey stripes.
The vehicle rides on Black Rhino Warlord wheels wrapped in Comforser CF 1100 all-terrain tires. At the rear, you'll come across a carrier with a custom-made aluminum cargo box, as well as a spare tire carrier/ladder combo.
Climb on top of the rig, and you'll discover a rack holding a Fiamma F80S awning with an integrated light, and solar panels.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Built Campervans There are a couple of flares on the van's sides. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south. This rig's CJL side pods are color matched to the van's paint and come with windows with sliding screens.
Other notable mods are aluminum bars all around the vehicle with integrated LED light pods, a water fill-up point, and a shore power connection. There are also two high beam lights attached to the roof bar.
On the inside, Custom Built Campervans had to strip out everything to make room for the new interior. And it does look much better than how it used to before (see images in gallery). What's more, it has a closed layout, with a wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for an oak slatted ceiling with recessed LED light strips, wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring, and grey laminated cabinetry.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Built Campervans They also chose some distinctive touches, such as an acrylic backsplash with a printed picture depicting a lion. Moreover, the look is complemented by some oak elements, such as the window frames or oak butcher block countertops, and grey couch upholstery with orange accents.
The dividing wall has a decently sized headliner compartment, as well as a large window so you can see from one area to another.
The first thing you'll see as you slide open the main door is one of the two kitchen units, positioned right by the divider wall. It offers a Thetford oven, a dual-burner induction stovetop, a flip-up table that can be used outside, three cupboards, and a drawer.
Straight ahead of the entrance, the builders devised one of the most sought-after amenities in premium camper vans: a bathroom. Hidden behind a waterproof retractable door, the bathroom boasts a Thetford toilet, a custom stainless steel shower tray, a shower, an overhead vanity compartment, and a Maxxair Dome vent fan.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Built Campervans The bathroom has a unique finish: the entire back wall has an acrylic print made from a picture that the customer took while on holiday.
Next, we have the other kitchen unit on the driver's side. It has a tall double-opening Dometic fridge with a tiny freezer compartment and a deep stainless steel sink with a cutting board cover.
A variety of storage compartments are available on both sides, including cupboards, drawers, and cabinets.
On the opposite side, Custom Built Campervans added an additional counter offering more surface area and a variety of storage spots. This is also where you'll discover most of the controls for the rig's utilities, including heating controls and a customizable SavvyVan touchscreen display for controlling power and water.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Built Campervans A cabinet integrated into the counter accommodates the Victron power system. Its highlights are a 460 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. You can use three charging sources: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging via the alternator while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank, and an outdoor shower. The last important utility system in this rig is an overhead A/C unit that can quickly cool off the interior when needed.
The rear part of the interior is occupied by a spacious seating area. It has a massive U-shaped couch with a table in the middle. Five people could easily fit here. Furthermore, you get storage cubbies behind the couch backrests.
You can turn the couch into a small sleeping arrangement – all you need to do is drop the table to the same height as the benches and rearrange the cushions.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Built Campervans However, this is not the main sleeping arrangement – you'll find that one right above. It's an elevator bed that can be raised or lowered at the press of a button. Lower it all the way down, and filler cushions on the sides extend the sleeping arrangement to make use of the entire interior width.
All in all, Custom Built Campervans drastically transformed this MAN TGE van into an aesthetically pleasing, super practical home on wheels. It's fascinating how much stuff the company managed to pack inside it.

Black-on-Pink Range Rover Looks Naughty, Wants You To Pay for It
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec
Even though it may no longer be the first choice when it comes to luxury-oriented SUVs for the rich and famous, as some of the one percents have opted for something else, the Range Rover remains an emblematic ride, and you can instantly tell that someone is loaded if they own one, especially an L460.
The latter is the codename of the fifth generation, which may not have started to show its age yet, but it is already four years old. It was unveiled in the fourth-quarter of 2021, and it hit the assembly line at the Solihull factory in the United Kingdom the following year. It also comes to life at Pune, in India, and it is based on the MLA Flex platform. Thus, it shares its nuts and bolts with the smaller Range Rover Sport, as both utilize this construction.
Designed by Gerry McGovern, who has also left his mark on numerous other vehicles from Land Rover over the years, the latest Range Rover is offered with standard four-wheel drive. Depending on where it is sold, you can have it with a straight-six turbo mild-hybrid, a twin-turbocharged 4.4-liter V8, a plug-in hybrid straight-six, and a diesel. Moreover, there is also an electric derivative out based on the same platform, aimed at deep-pocketed enthusiasts who have always craved for a zero-emission Range Rover.
Now that we have reminded ourselves about the Range Rover and, more specifically, the modern-day fifth-generation model, it is time to move on to the pictured example, which is looking for a new home as we speak. The vehicle in question is located in Miami, Florida, and while it may not stand out that much on the outside, where it is mostly black, save for the emblems at the front and rear, it definitely does just that when opening the door.
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec Actually, you do not have to open the door to see the interior, because you can zoom in through the windows, and you will quickly realize that it is on the very special side of things. The vendor says it is custom, and it is dominated by pink. Thus, pretty much everywhere you look, from the dashboard panel to the steering wheel, and from the door cards to the seats and center console, you will see the new leather upholstery.
The pillars and headliner are also pink, and by the looks of it, they have been wrapped in Alcantara rather than leather. The seatbelts remain black, and it is nice to see that the Range Rover emblem on the steering wheel soldiers on. The latter has a two-spoke design, plenty of buttons on it, and some metal trim. The latter is also visible throughout the interior, and everything else appears to soldier on from the factory.
That is, unless we have missed something, and we reckon we didn’t. Actually, we did, but on the outside, and here, we mean the wheels. The new alloys have a turbine-like shape, and they are larger than the stock ones. Thus, they have clearly come from the aftermarket world. We would have liked to tell you the size and what tires hug them, but this information hasn’t been released by the vendor, which also mentions the full blackout package.
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec That’s not that only thing mentioned in the rather short caption on social media that accompanies the pictures shared in the gallery, as the dealer, @limitedspec on Instagram, also reveals that this is a 2025 model year Range Rover . Moreover, the luxury-oriented SUV has in the region of 19,000 miles (~30,500 km) on the clock, and while it is not exactly brand new, it definitely looks very good both inside and out.
But how much does something like this cost in today’s used car market? Well, the average selling price of the 2025 Range Rover SE, which is the configuration of the pictured example, spans between $80,000 and $135,000. Trade-ins tend to go from $80,000 to over $90,000, and the resale value of such a thing is more than $90,000, depending on the powertrain. And guess what? The vendor hasn’t mentioned the oily bits at all.
However, the charging port located on the other side of the fuel filler cap tells us that we are dealing with a plug-in hybrid. And it is likely the P550e, which packs an electrified straight-six turbocharged mill, with 550 hp (560 ps/410 kW ) and 590 lb-ft (800 Nm) of torque combined. The latest Range Rover SE kicks off at $113,300 new, excluding destination, options, and dealer fees.
So, how much do you think this Range Rover, with its new wheels and custom interior, is? A lot of money. In fact, the asking price at the time of writing was $179,980. But if you were searching for a used Range Rover and came across this example, would you really cough out $180K for it? You know what to do next if you said yes, don't you? My First Six Races in Gran Turismo 7 After the New Spec IV Update
26 photos
Photo: autoevolution
Forgive me officer, cause I have sinned. My left foot and right foot have once again coordinated with my hands to make the car go sideways against my common sense. At least it happened I a remote area with no traffic and no pedestrians, so that has to count for something right?
Over the past 12 months, I’ve behaved for roughly 99% of the time I was behind the steering wheel. I only tend to lose sight of the promise I made myself to keep it to the track when I’m in the Mazda RX-8 and it’s raining outside.
To my defense, there was a huge global drift day celebration going on when I performed a 360 degree turn, and I immediately felt ashamed of having done so. Well, I’d be lying if I said there wasn’t some happiness involved, as I’m genuinely desperate to finish working on my RX-7 and take it to the racetrack.
I just know there’s no way I could do everything I want in it and still keep my license. Having Gran Turismo 7 around with its latest update was of some relief though, and I’m particularly excited about having the Sugo International Racing Course in the game.
I’ve saved the new Circuit Experience for last, as first I wanted to complete the new Weekly Challenges and see what kind of a cool car I would unlock from the 6-Star Roulette Ticket.
Special Race Photo: autoevolution It’s not often that the Week’s Special Race is the first of the five challenges. It’s usually somewhere in the middle. Perhaps I underestimated the impact the Citroën 2 CV 6 Charleston would have on the global GT7 fanbase.
For a moment, I thought about using the bone stock version, just so I wouldn’t crush my opponents. Then I realized I wasn’t about to drive three laps around the Kyoto Driving Park (Miyabi layout) with under 30 horsepower on tap. After going for most of the upgrades available for the ‘80s machine, it now had 136 bhp and weighed about as much as two and a half Aprilia RS 660 motorcycles.
SS tires were a must, and I immediately found an interesting livery for it browsing through the 10 pages available right now. Despite the extra power, the Citroen was nice to drive, and my only complaint is that the 4-speed gearbox is limited to 93 mph (150 kph).
I might genuinely try that Honda Integra engine swap, although I’m certain keeping it NA is the only way to avoid ruining the balance of the car for good. I scored 48,000 credits (Clean Race Bonus included) after two and a half minutes of driving, plus the extra 100,000 credits you get as part of the Weekly Challenges system.
European Sunday Cup 400 Photo: autoevolution I probably spent about an hour at Sugo the day it went live in GT7, practicing for the newest Time Trial. I can’t say I’ve mastered it, but I already feel at home pushing any car to its (or my) limit. The European Sunday Cup 400 called for the Ferrari F355 Berlinetta, as I had a blast experiencing it with no upgrades.
I knew a pair of stickier tires was all it needed to limit the oversteer, and it worked like a charm. Sure, I was a bit over the suggested PP limit (570), but I don’t regret one moment of it. People have already been hard at work creating custom liveries for the car, and I found a nice one in yellow.
I can guarantee you don’t need more power to enjoy driving the F355, and three laps went by way too fast. It reminded me of something one of the chefs (Gennaro Contaldo) I’ve been following on YouTube used to say “Why am I cooking so good?”.
My fastest lap was a 1:34.392, which is roughly six seconds faster than my previous attempt and all just by changing the tires and getting more practice. Five minutes of driving will get you 63,000 credits, if you can claim the Clean Race Bonus as well.
The Silvia Sisters Photo: autoevolution I’ve been playing Gran Turismo 7 for years and still haven’t finished it 100%. I also haven’t bought all of the vehicles in the Legends Car Dealership. Frankly, the new Concierge service does nothing to help me with that, as it just made getting those cars even more expensive.
Thanks for nothing! Anyway, what I wanted to say that this Silvia Sisters event around the Deep Forest Raceway is one of the few events in the game where I haven’t previously managed to emerge victorious.
My best result thus far was a P2 finish, and I had no plans of struggling for the win again. I bought a non-turbo PS13 and once again went overboard with all the upgrades, before realizing I could get an SR20DET engine swap.
With 331 bhp and a total weight of 2,065 lbs/937 kg, running on SS tires, I was just “slightly” over the suggested PP Level (620 vs 500). The Tomica livery is a great match for the build, and winning after five minutes was a piece of cake. Scoring just 45,000 credits for the effort wasn’t so fun though.
World Rally Challenge Group B Photo: autoevolution I only had a Group B Subaru in my garage, and I’ve probably used it for the past two or three events in this class already. I needed a change. Instead of the Concierge, wouldn’t it have been nicer if Polyphony would have provided a Filter option to buy new cars based on their category?
I went for a Honda NSX Gr.B Rally Car, but I wasn’t 100% enthusiastic about it all as these events are best kept off-road. Ten laps at Willow Springs International Raceway will have an impact on both your tires and your gas tank, so keep in mind you’ll need a strategy for the two.
To the person who came up with the “Doritos” livery, thank you very much! I’m a big fan of both the nachos and the design, but I just had to paint the wheels white for the job. Another NSX was up in P2, with the Pikes Peak Quattro in P1, but that only lasted for three laps.
There’s quite a bit of “dancing” involved given the way the suspension is set up on this car, and my front left tire was constantly in distress throughout the race. Scoring 65,000 credits after 14 minutes wasn’t ideal, but at least the final event will be better from that perspective.
World Touring Car 800 Photo: autoevolution It’s been a while since we last had a race at the Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve in Canada! And I remembered the competition was fairly stiff in these ones, with 19 opponents and 12 laps to go. I was tempted to drive one of the Porsche GT3 machines again, especially after seeing the teaser for the new Mission S.
But I thought I’d spend more time with the new Mazda RX-Vision GT3 EVO instead. The Renown livery was the obvious choice, and I was in P6 after four laps. I missed the pit lane entry and had to tone it down a bit to Map 6 to “survive” on how little fuel I had left.
It took me 10 laps to get into the lead, which should tell you something about how difficult this race is. After almost 21 minutes of driving, the car in P2 (a Ferrari 296 GT3) was only 17 seconds behind!
But it was all worth it, as I walked with 170,000 more credits to my name and the Honda NSX GT500 ‘08 (which is one of my favorite cars in the game). I’ll need to test it at Sugo soon, but first I had an encounter with a more modern GT500 machine.
Circuit Experience: Sugo International Racing Course Photo: autoevolution The new Circuit Experience will put you behind the wheel of the GT-R NISMO GT500 ‘16, for four sectors and one complete lap attack. The target for Gold sits at 1:13.200, while Bronze will take at least 1:20.400.
These targets should tell you how much faster this GT500 race car is compared to the Xiaomi Vision Gran Turismo, despite the EV having roughly 2,000 horsepower to work with.
I scored Bronze on my first or second attempt at Sugo, and found myself almost falling in love with this track while doing so.
I might use it as my next test ground for another Engine Swap story, even though I’ve told myself to stay away from those several times before. Also, while earning 200,000 credits for Bronze was nice, I’ll probably go at it again chasing for the grand prize.

Meet the Carbon Fiber Beast: The Ultimate One-of-One Mansory P820 Linea D’Arabo
19 photos
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory
Is there such a thing as having too many modded Mercedes-AMG G 63 SUVs? Well, not if you’re name is Mansory, as this tuner has dropped a large number of upgraded G-Wagens over the years, and quite a few of them in recent times.
Our previous encounter with one of these included the so-called Grand Entree , which is a G-Wagen in the AMG configuration with suicide rear doors, and a few other aftermarket goodies. And even if it may not be named the Grand Entree, the one pictured above has this mod, too, in addition to others, and it is one monstrous-looking machine with extra oomph.
It’s christened the Mansory P820 Linea D’Arabo , just like other similar takes on the Mercedes-AMG G 63 and not only, though this one is said to be a bespoke creation. It definitely looks like something that would come from Mansory’s portfolio, and if it weren’t for some upgrades, and the typical logos, one might actually mistake it for a Brabus. And that’s a compliment in this case, because this machine does not look kitschy at all, this writer thinks.
Some of the novelties on the outside include the fender flares with some sculpted elements on them for a more predatory look, the new hood with its vented design, the different front bumper that features new vents and claw-like extra daytime running lights on the sides, and the grille. The latter does not follow the typical Panamericana pattern, as it features a different look, and is decorated with the Mansory logo in the middle, an another Mansory emblem on the side.
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory Moreover, this Mercedes-AMG G 63 has extra panels on the front fenders, front and rear doors, and rear three-quarter panels, which make it loot a lot more muscular. The door mirror casings are new, from what we can tell, and there is a roof-mounted piece above the front windscreen with extra lights, and another one at the rear, which is a wing. We can also see some rear pillar attachments, as well as an entirely new bumper and a diffuser with multi fins and blades on the sides attached to it.
Besides these, the Mansory P820 Linea D’Arabo in question benefits from a custom spare wheel holder attached to the rear door, which also has an extra panel on the lower part, what seems to be an extra brake light in the middle of the diffuser, and another set of taillights below the OEM ones, mounted on each side of the new bumper. The wheels are also on the special side of things, and they do not look out of place at all, and the tailpipe trim is also new.
Inside, this Mercedes-AMG G 63 has a similar theme to the exterior. The upholstery is new, and so is the trim. The steering wheel has been partially wrapped in suede, and also sports forged carbon on it. We can see some black and gray details here and there, as well as Mansory’s backlit logo on the custom door cards and on other elements. Power running boards with illumination improve ingress and egress, and the rear doors have a suicide-style opening, as we already told you.
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory There is no starry sky headliner on deck, and that’s a compliment, by the way. The rear captain’s chairs are decorated with Mansory’s logo on the headrest cushions and on the seatbacks, and they are separated by a large center console that features a screen on it, and probably offers some extra storage. Pretty much everywhere you look, you can see something new, and the attention to detail is definitely worth mentioning.
The P820 in its name tells us that this machine has 820 metric horsepower. That’s 808 brake horsepower and 603 kilowatts, and it represents a very healthy jump over the standard powertrain, which kicks out 577 bhp (585 ps/430 kW ), and is officially rated at 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque. Mansory hasn’t said anything about the performance of this tuned Mercedes-AMG G 63, but with no outside intervention, the model hits 62 mph (100 kph )in 4.3 seconds, and reaches up to 149 mph (240 kph) with the optional AMG Driver’s Pack.
Due to the exposed carbon fiber components, widebody kit, new wheels, custom interior, performance enhancements, and other things, the Mansory P820 Linea D’Arabo pictured in the gallery above can easily stand out from the crowd, even in a sea of supercars, or other modified Mercedes-AMG G 63 SUVs. It’s unknown whether this ride is searching for a new home, if it was a special commission, or if it is a simple marketing tool for the time being, but rest assured, a lot of money has gone into it.
In fact, if it were listed for grabs, we wouldn’t be surprised to learn that it costs well over half a million bucks, and probably close to one million dollars. Would you ever get one of these if money were the least of your concerns? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kourosh Mansory (@_kourosh_mansory)

S650 Ford Racing Mustang Cobra R Takes the new Mustang Dark Horse SC in a Virtually Crazy Direction
9 photos
Photo: abimelecdesign / Instagram
The Ford Motor Company has crafted a few new and cool models for the iconic Ford Mustang lineup – the 795-horsepower Dark Horse SC and 815-hp Mustang GTD being chief among them. While we wait to see if the Blue Oval also adds a new sedan body style, let’s also imagine something else thanks to a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
Abimelec Arellano, a virtual artist better known as " abimelecdesign " on social media, has prepared the newest wishful-thinking project - a cool American coupe. The thing is that this pixel master has a knack for the Blue Oval side of America’s automotive market. He recently gave us a Ford Taurus SHO Saleen sedan, a Ford Crown Victoria Ute with steelies, and even a Ford Crown Victoria with an Australian passport, among others.
But now he’s not interested in sedans – only feisty muscle cars of the coupe variety. He explains that he thinks the “new Mustang Dark Horse SC is incredible— 2.9 seconds to 60 and a bunch of track-ready hardware, plus a very distinctive body kit and aerodynamics. I love that, and I love it even more because underneath the Dark Horse badges, carbon fiber wheels and carbon fiber inserts, I can see something else that had been missing from Mustangs for a while,” aka the ‘Cobra stance.’
According to his vision, the Cobra models from the Ford Motor Company from the 1990s and 2000s “had a very unique stance— whether you’re talking about the Fox-bodies or the more extreme Cobra Terminator, they always had that ‘chunkier,’ heavier, aggressive presence.” So, when Ford unleashed the 795-hp Dark Horse SC, “the overall look just screamed Cobra stance to me, more specifically, one of the most iconic Mustangs of all time: the 2000 Cobra R .”
As such, he decided to bring out the “essence” of that model to CGI light, via some digital modifications plastered over the Dark Horse SC: “the chin spoiler is deeper, lower, and the side aero elements are gone. The carbon fiber inserts are all painted, along with replacing the grille horse with the Cobra.” Additionally, the artist reimagined the five-spoke Cobra R wheels, created thicker and lower side exhausts, and now there are side exhausts, of course.
Last but not least, the CGI presentation is based on the “wonderful” Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2 video game, and the “rear diffuser is hollowed out where the exhausts used to be to move more air, and on top of the rear sits the controversial Cobra R wing. Of course, it is not exactly a Cobra R wing; this is way more curved and contoured to the body of the S650, but keeps the styling almost identical to the original.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Abimelec Arellano (@abimelecdesign)

Mazda Soul Red Sedan Virtually Steals the Cuorerosso From Alfa Romeo, Hopefully the Hybrid V6 Too
7 photos
Photo: lsdesignsrl / Instagram
Back in September, the French-Italian-American carmaker Stellantis firmly announced its intention to rule the 2026 Paris Motor Show taking place between October 12 and 18 at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles in France with over 60 show vehicles, nine of them being concept cars.
The company even organized a ‘The Night Before’ event, like in the golden old days of automotive shows before the pandemics, and showcased the most important six concepts ahead of the press day to steal the red carpet’s spotlight. They were right to do so because they had cool things to showcase: the Citroen 2CV Concept, a preview of the upcoming return of the iconic 2CV made as an accessible, fully electric model.
There were also the DS F3VER design-led concept to explore the future of the DS Automobiles specialty brand with a possible return of the DS3 model, the ultra-quirky Fiat Multiplay, which reimagined the much-chagrined Multipla as a morphing truck-minivan, the Opel STX dedicated to the revival of the station wagon sector, plus the Peugeot RCZ Vision based on the new STLA One platform.
However, one of the concepts topped all the others – and not because they were uncool. Instead, Alfa Romeo has returned to its former glorious self with the Cuorerosso, a concept car that will probably never morph into a series production model unlike the other five, but nevertheless is painstakingly showing that Alfa still has the design knowledge of making astonishingly beautiful cars.
This ‘sedan’ with a shifting paint – red, of course – has a striking structural feature: the door layout. Like the new Genesis GV90 Neolun , we are dealing with a B-pillarless design and coach rear doors. Also, very importantly, the concept previews an electrified revolution for the iconic 2.9-liter twin-turbocharged V6 engine used in the Quadrifoglio models, mixed with Alfa Romeo's Q4 all-wheel-drive system and a lightweight carbon fiber driveshaft.
If Stellantis dared to put the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso right now into production, it would immediately clash with the likes of the Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, Ferrari Luce, as well as the newly announced Jaguar Type 01, providing a hybridized alternative to the new crop of ultra-luxury high-performance sedans!
Too bad that Stellantis won’t dare that, right? Well, some folks have found other solutions – including a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, Luca Serafini, a virtual automotive designer based in Modena, Italy (aka ' lsdesignsrl ' on social media), has imagined an unofficial, hypothetical Mazda sedan as an alternative to the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso.
The pixel master basically hijacked the stunning design of the Alfa Romeo concept car and swapped the ‘scudetto’ front fascia with the characteristic visage of Mazda models, modifying the LED headlights in the process to better harmonize with the rest of the body of the coach-door sedan. Around the back, the changes are minimal, with the Mazda script instead of Alfa Romeo and a single smaller exhaust instead of the double one used by the Italian concept car.
Mazda has some great powrtrains, but Alfa's hybrid V6 would be an even better fit inside the belly of this streamlined beast, especially if the Italians push the electrified package to more than 700 combined ponies, right? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Luca Serafini (@lsdesignsrl)

The more than $600 million judgment in a Texas court case against C.H. Robinson has been affirmed by the judge that heard the case.
Judge Dianne Jones of Dallas County Court on Friday affirmed the July verdict of $604,025,000 handed down in July against C.H. Robinson (NASDAQ: CHRW) as a result of a fatal accident that killed three persons in March 2021.
One of the three persons killed in the wreck was Gorgonio Gonzalez, an employee driver of carrier Lupus Superior that was hired by C.H. Robinson to move a load for Arizona Beverages. His death made finding the cause of the accident difficult to ascertain.
The lead named plaintiff in the case is the estate of Jennifer Lipe, represented by Peyton Lipe. Jennifer Lipe was one of the persons killed in the crash that occurred in Jackson, Mississippi, though the case was heard in Texas because that is the headquarters of Lupus Superior.
The case of Lipe vs. Lupus Superior, the carrier hired by C.H. Robinson, is problematic for C.H. Robinson on two key fronts.
One is the $600-million plus verdict. While there have been nuclear verdicts in trucking larger than that–though not many–there is no known precedent for a verdict of that size against a publicly-traded company with an investment-grade credit rating and an end-second quarter balance sheet of $5.8 billion. Some of the larger verdicts were handed down against companies that were effectively ghosts and didn’t participate in their defense.
(It is notable that the second quarter balance sheet for C.H. Robinson listed cash and cash equivalents of $154.9 million, far below the Lipe award).
Who’s in control?
But the other major issue for C.H. Robinson, and by extension the brokerage community in general, is the jury’s finding, in response to a question in the jury’s charge, that driver Gonzalez was “operating the vehicle in the furtherance of a mission for the benefit of C.H. Robinson and subject to control by C.H. Robinson as to the details of the mission.”
If that finding is upheld on appeal, it means the brokerage industry would have gone in just a few months from liability protection under the Federal Aviation Administration Authorization Act (F4A) being blown away in May by the Supreme Court’s Montgomery decision , to a precedent that may be set by Lipe vs. Lupus Superior that the driver at a carrier is effectively controlled by the brokerage that hired the trucking company.
In a prepared statement released late Friday following the affirmation, C.H. Robinson reiterated several of the same points that it made not only when the initial decision was handed down in July but also in various forums since then.
The company expressed sympathy for the “profound loss suffered by the families in this case.”
“But C.H. Robinson did not cause or contribute to the accident, and accountability must be grounded in the facts and the law,” Dorothy Capers, chief legal officer at C.H. Robinson, said in the prepared statement.
Capers’ statement brought up a question facing brokers in the post-Montgomery landscape: what constitutes a hiring process that can protect them?
Dorothy Capers of C.H. Robinson
She pointed out, as has been done before, that Lupus Superior had a Satisfactory rating from the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) and had “safely delivered nearly 270 loads for our customers.”
“The carrier is an independent company and the driver worked for them,” Capers said in the statement. “C.H. Robinson does not employ drivers.”
“The extreme nature of this judgment underscores why a clear national standard for what constitutes a safe carrier is needed now,” Capers’ statement added. “America’s freight network should not be governed by safety standards determined after the fact, state by state and courtroom by courtroom.”
It is an issue that has been raised publicly by the Transportation Intermediaries Association. In June, it called for federal action of some kind to determine what a broker can rely upon to protect itself when hiring brokers.
The size of the payout does not end with the $604 million. As TD Cowen’s Jason Seidl noted in an analyst report released soon after news spread of the affirmation, there is also approximately $107 million in pre-judgement interest affirmed by Judge Jones.
“We believe the substantial interest charge was less appreciated by investors and drove weakness in trading immediately after the judgment was entered, though this was included in the plaintiff’s originally proposed judgment,” Seidl wrote.
The interest rate being applied to the judgment is 6.75%.
“Assuming CHRW moves to appeal and this results in a multi-year process, this would imply an even larger compounded charge if appeal is unsuccessful,” Seidl added.
C.H. Robinson, Seidl wrote, has a “non-trivial incentive to settle this lawsuit eventually if appeal sees adverse developments, though overturning the vicarious liability ruling (where C.H. Robinson was found to control the driver) in appeal is likely to remain a first preference.”

Porsche’s Mission S Gets New Wheels and Tires for More Virtual Street Cred
12 photos
Photo: Instagram | Vossen
It may be the new Tesla Roadster’s demonstration that everyone talks about, but this hasn’t been the only important debut of the week. If we can call it a debut, because the EV will go into production in 2028, according to the company, and we all know what that means when it comes to Teslas, don’t we?
That it will probably be delayed a few more times before it finally heads into production. After all, the automaker decided to put a pin on it several times so far. Let’s not forget that it was supposed to hit the roads in 2020 originally, and that was three years after it debuted as a study. And speaking of that, it looks different from the concept, and some have called it the offspring of the Tesla Cybertruck and a previous-generation supercar.
Now, we are heading into a different realm, so we’d better end it here and move on to the real reason behind this story, which is all about the Porsche Mission S . Uncovered at about the same time as the new Tesla Roadster’s demonstrations, the is not a full production car. Far from it, actually, because what we have here is a concept, albeit a very nice one that proves that the Zuffenhausen brand continues to do what it does best, as instead of chasing after crossovers and SUVs, it has just dropped another super sports car.
Even if it is nothing more than a study, it is a very important one for the automaker, because it represents a first official glimpse into a future super sports model that will clearly sit above the 911. Not only that, but it also previews the company’s future design identity, and to be honest, it is not bad at all, is it?
Photo: Porsche The design is on the dramatic side of things, especially at the rear, where it features a radiator fan in the middle of the engine cover, which has been clearly inspired by the Porsche 917 . A flowing rear wing is also on deck, incorporated into the body work, and there is also an uncommon diffuser at the rear. Four stacked exhaust pipes are part of the design, just like the ultra-thin taillights, and the Porsche lettering between them.
The styling at the rear may be quite dramatic, but at the front, it looks quite familiar. If anything, one can easily mistake it for a track-focused 911 that costs a lot of money, and that’s not necessarily a bad thing, this writer believes. It has a long nose with a large air intake in the lower part of the bumper, a sharp apron with blades on the sides, a vented front hood, familiar-looking headlights, and a roof scoop.
Porsche’s Mission S Concept therefore remains easily identifiable as something that comes from the Zuffenhausen company, and even if the paint on its body has barely dried out, it has already fallen into the hands of the rendering world. Actually, it is the wheel-making rendering world this time, because several wheelmakers have dropped CGIs of this machine that imagine it sitting on various alloys.
Photo: Instagram | Vossen In this case, it is Vossen that shared these digital illustration on its social media channels just a few hours after the car’s official unveiling, revealing that the alloys in question are called the G2-13T. The G2 series is also available in the 01, 10, 11T, 12,, and 14 configurations, each one stretching from 18 to 22 inches in diameter, with different lip configurations, and a few other options, the company’s official website reveals.
We do not know the size of the wheels on which this imagined Porsche Mission S sits, but if we were to guess, we’d say that they are probably the 22-inch proposal. The automaker says that the wheels of the real Mission S “ draw on an iconic design from the Porsche history and develop it further, ” mentioning “ the dial-style wheels of the 928, ” and adding that it is “ more than just a reinterpretation of a design motif, ” as it is “ a link between the sports cars of yesterday and the driver’s cars of tomorrow. ”
Despite being uncovered, we do not know much about the oily bits of the Porsche Mission S, though we can tell you that it features a read mid-engine setup, and that’s great news for those who do not necessarily fancy electric vehicles. Recent reports indicate that the Zuffenhausen auto marque is working on a punchy new eight-cylinder boxer engine for its upcoming flagship model, and this is expected to be the production version of the Mission S, so Porsche looks like it has a winner in its future super sports car stable.
Now, we are not here to praise the study , nor to remind you about it, as this story is all about the rendered model sitting on new wheels, as we already told you.
